newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Dec 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- As Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh declared the government's policies to Parliament yesterday, two leading Cabinet members were engaged in a verbal clash behind the House speaker's podium over the division of work at the Communications Ministry. Deputy Prime Minister Montree Pongpanit has threatened to pull out of the government coalition after his heated quarrel with Communications Minister Suwat Liptapanlop. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Chart Pattana Party leader Chatichai Choonhavan has switched into high gear in his role as top government adviser, leading a meeting between party ministers and former Japanese prime minister Toshiki Kaifu, during which the Thais called for funds to construct a second Mekong bridge. The bridge will connect Thailand's Mukdahan province to Savannakhet in Laos. (THE NATION)

- The Democrat Party has urged police to investigate a police general's claim there is a major gambling den operating under police protection in Bangkok. Democrat leader Chuan Leekpai has said instead of denying the claim and seeking disciplinary action against the outspoken officer, the police leadership should set up a committee to investigate his allegation and make its findings clear to the public. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government has voiced concern over getting involved in the private sector's proposed boycott of European products as a retaliatory measure against recent European Union (EU) decisions surrounding Thai agricultural products. The proposal was put forward by Thai frozen food exporters following the EU decision to cancel the Generalised System of Preferences on Thai agricultural items, which including fruit and vegetables, seafood and canned food. The measure will come into effective next month. (BUSINESS DAY)

- MasterCall (Thailand) vice chairman will fly to Beijing today in a bid to end confusion over the company's mobile phone concession in the Chinese capital. The company's vice chairman says he has spoken to officials of China Unicom, the government telecom regulator that granted the concession, and they say they are unaware of any cancellation. (BANGKOK POST)

- Chatichai Choonhavan, chief adviser to the prime minister on international relations and economic affairs, plans to lead a series of roadshows to bolster Thailand's image in Japan, India and eastern Europe starting next month. He will also help the prime minister tackle problems in the property and export sectors and restructure manufacturing industries by proposing subcommittees for each task. (THE NATION)
